title: Unit 2: Monera, Protoctista and Fungi
blurb: Three kingdoms of living things: bacteria, protozoa and algae, and fungi.
sort: Its largest group is the bacteria
It can be autotrophic or heterotrophic
It is classified by shape: cocci, bacilli, vibrios, spirochaeta
It reproduces only asexually, by binary fission
It is a heterotrophic, unicellular eukaryote
It is classified by how it moves: flagellates, ciliates, rhizopods
It moves with lots of short cilia
Its cells have chloroplasts and a cell wall
It is classified as green, red or brown (multicellular types)
Multicellular forms are attached to the sea floor or river bed
It can be unicellular, living free or in colonies, or multicellular
It has a cell wall but no chloroplasts
It reproduces by budding (unicellular) or by spores (multicellular)
Its groups are yeasts, moulds and mushroom-forming fungi
Its body is a mycelium made of hyphae
A fruiting body releases its spores
It is heterotrophic and generally attached to the ground or to other living things

cloze: Monera cells are {prokaryotic}, which means they have no nucleus.
Protozoa that move with pseudopods are called {rhizopods}.
The body of a fungus is the {mycelium}, made of thin threads called {hyphae}.
Algae are {autotrophic} because their cells contain {chloroplasts}.

clues: I have no chloroplasts, so I am heterotrophic.
I am one of the protozoa.
I move with lots of short hairs.
I am a kind of bacterium.
I am attached to the sea floor and I can be green, red or brown.
I have a cell wall but no chloroplasts.
My body is a mycelium and I release spores.
I am one of the protozoa.
I move with a long whip-like tail.

order.title: Binary fission
steps: The DNA of the mother cell is copied
A new wall forms across the middle

order.title: Budding in yeast
steps: A small bud forms on the parent cell
The bud separates from the parent
The bud becomes a new yeast cell
